instructions: Review the immutable README, mapping contract, Lava deploy, SQL verifier, and static test before adaptation.
Create the target Connection Request attributes and complete every required value in the deploy's ADAPTATION REQUIRED block.

Run the deploy twice and require stable reuse plus zero invalid Create Connection Request references.
Review the workflow in Rock, then assign it manually as the registration template's Registrant Workflow.
Submit a marked test registration through the real registration experience and run the read-only verifier.
Document retry and backfill duplicate behavior before processing any existing registrants.
known_limitations: The sanitized deployment has not been executed unchanged against every supported Rock release or plugin combination.
The native registration trigger is expected to launch once per new registrant; manual reruns and backfills require an explicit duplicate policy.
The example includes one generic mapped value and must be extended carefully for additional fields and field-type normalization.
Connection Request attribute qualifiers vary by local Connection configuration and must be created and permissioned before deployment.
An empty registration campus remains empty; the recipe intentionally does not substitute the person's primary campus.
learnings: Registrant-scoped automation should use the template's Registrant Workflow and consume RegistrationRegistrantId rather than guessing from registrar or person context.
Create Connection Request falls back to the person's primary campus when no Campus Attribute is configured, so registration campus must be wired explicitly when it is authoritative.
Capture the created request in a workflow attribute before later native actions copy request attributes.
Store the source Registration ID and construct local links when rendering instead of persisting environment-specific URLs.
Use stable ForeignKeys and re-query canonical IDs after every modify operation so rerunnable deploys do not depend on transient return objects.
Validate that all action-setting attribute GUIDs belong to the same WorkflowType; stale cross-workflow references can survive copied configuration.
Keep deployment SQL read-only and use native Rock actions for runtime writes.
Treat retries and backfills as a separate reviewed workflow because unconditionally rerunning Create Connection Request can create duplicates.
outcomes: Each newly submitted registrant can launch a workflow that creates a native Connection Request.
The request records the source Registration ID without persisting an environment-specific admin URL.

A nonproduction environment and marked test registration for end-to-end validation.

Review marked test Connection Requests manually; do not bulk-delete requests or AttributeValues through this recipe.
Disable or remove the temporary admin deployment endpoint after rollback verification.

The reference does not delete or merge existing requests and must not be used as a bulk cleanup tool.

instructions: Review the immutable README, workflow contract, source, and static test before adapting the recipe.
Create a dedicated verification workflow and configure its SMS action to clear the plain Code attribute immediately after delivery.

Create POST-only start, check, and final-submit endpoints with only the required Lava commands and anti-CSRF behavior; enable Sql and WorkflowActivate for start, then Sql and ModifyWorkflow for check and final submission.
Keep endpoint SQL query-only and use ModifyWorkflow for Attempts, Verified, and ConsumedAt state changes.
Supply every local configuration value without introducing fallback production IDs or routes.

Integrate the final-submit recheck immediately before the protected form action, use only its server-resolved alias context, and make the protected operation idempotent with protectedActionIdempotencyKey.
Add anonymous traffic controls, monitoring, retention decisions, privacy review, and an accessible non-SMS path before launch.
known_limitations: SMS possession is not complete identity proofing, account authentication, or phishing-resistant MFA.
The public package is a reference integration and has not been live-tested unchanged in a generic Rock instance.
Exact match fields can exclude legitimate people with stale or shared data and require an accessible fallback.
Context.Request.UserHostAddress may identify a reverse proxy unless the target environment provides a trusted client-address mechanism.

ModifyWorkflow does not provide atomic compare-and-set behavior; concurrent final requests can both pass the recheck, so the protected operation must reject a repeated protectedActionIdempotencyKey or return the first result.
A strict exactly-once requirement needs a purpose-built Rock action or API with an application-layer transaction; this reference intentionally contains no SQL writes.
learnings: Treat anonymous recognition as a persisted, bounded server challenge rather than as a browser state transition.
Fail closed on ambiguous person matches instead of selecting the oldest or lowest-ID candidate.
Return an opaque session for every start request so browser response structure does not reveal whether a person exists.
Never let a browser-supplied person or alias identifier establish verified applicant context.
Bind each challenge to an intended action, enforce expiration and attempt limits, and make the final protected operation idempotent with the challenge session.
Use query-only SQL for complex challenge lookup and hashing while routing workflow state changes through ModifyWorkflow.
Separate the short-lived delivery code from durable audit state and make communication retention an explicit decision.
outcomes: Only one exact eligible person match can receive a challenge.
The browser receives an opaque challenge session but no person or alias identifier.
A verified challenge is bound to one intended action, expires, counts attempts, and supplies a stable idempotency key for the final protected operation.
The reference performs no SQL writes; workflow state changes use Rock's ModifyWorkflow command.
prerequisites: A dedicated Rock workflow type with the attributes and SMS delivery actions documented by the package.
A configured SMS transport and an explicit communication-history retention decision.
Permission to create secured Helix Lava Application POST endpoints and anonymous abuse controls.
A protected final operation that enforces idempotency using the supplied intended-action and session key.
A privacy and risk review for the form data used in exact matching.
rollback_steps: Disable the three Lava Application endpoints and remove their page/form integration.
Deactivate the verification workflow type or its SMS action to stop new messages.
Revert the protected form to its non-verified anonymous path; existing verification workflow rows can expire under the approved retention policy.

security.authentication: Anonymous form request plus possession of the SMS destination; this is not account authentication or identity proofing.
security.authorization: The challenge may authorize only its configured intended form action; workflow and communication administration remain restricted to appropriate staff roles.
notes: Zero or multiple person matches fail closed, and every start response uses the same browser-visible shape.
The browser never receives the matched person ID, alias ID, or alias GUID.
The final endpoint rechecks expiration, verification, intended action, and the best-effort consumed marker on the server, then supplies an idempotency key to the protected operation.
All SQL in the reference endpoints is query-only; Attempts, Verified, and ConsumedAt are written through ModifyWorkflow.
A six-digit code hash reduces accidental exposure but does not resist an attacker who can read the database; database controls, rate limits, expiration, and retention remain required.
SMS is vulnerable to interception and redirection and must not be described as strong identity proofing or phishing-resistant MFA.

summary: Optionally recognize an existing person during an anonymous Rock form using an exact unique match, persisted workflow challenge, bounded SMS code, Rock modify-command state writes, and an idempotent final action.
title: Workflow-Backed SMS Verification for Anonymous Rock Forms
use_cases: Optionally recognize a returning person during an anonymous registration or request form.
Prefill or associate a final form action only after phone-possession verification.
Keep short-lived verification state server-side without trusting browser-provided person identifiers.
validation_steps: Run python3 tests/static_contract.py from the recipe directory.
Confirm one exact eligible match sends one code while zero or multiple matches send none.
Confirm all start responses have the same status, message, timing envelope where practical, and field shape.
Confirm invalid, expired, over-attempt, wrong-action, already-verified, and consumed challenges fail safely.
Race two final submissions and confirm both receive the same protectedActionIdempotencyKey while the protected operation produces only one business result.
Scan every Lava source file and confirm no SQL UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE, or MERGE statement is present.
Inspect browser responses and confirm no person ID, alias ID, or alias GUID is present.
Confirm per-person, per-source, resend, and upstream anonymous traffic limits work through the real proxy path.
Confirm the plain Code workflow value is cleared and review any rendered SMS retained in communication history.
Confirm the protected final action cannot run by submitting only browser fields without a valid server-side challenge.
